newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN's Ekeus hopes for Iraqi missile accounting.
newsitem.headline: UN's Ekeus hopes for Iraqi missile accounting.

text.p: Chief U.N. weapons inspector Rolf Ekeus said Thursday it would be a "real achievement" if Iraq finally accounted for its missile potential when he visits Baghdad later this week.
"There is a very serious problem of missiles and the counting of missiles. That would be a major achivement if that could be settled," he said.

He was speaking to reporters after briefing the Security Council on his latest written report, issued last Friday, which said Iraq might still be hiding small but significant quantities of forbidden weapons, including missiles, chemical and biological warfare agents.
Ekeus, who in the past has said between six and 16 missiles remain unaccounted for, said they were capable of delivering biological or advanced high-quality chemical warfare agents.
"So it is not a theoretical or accounting problem. It is a real matter of life and death for the states in the region, and therefore we cannot rest until we have accounted for them," he added.
Ekeus leaves for Baghdad late on Thursday and arrives in the Iraqi capital on Saturday for meetings with Tareq Aziz, the Iraqi deputy prime minister.
